turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
Now let's check how resources (responses, chat completions) call into `Stream` / core APIPromise, and the higher-level lib streaming helpers.Now let's check chat/completions.ts for its streaming route, and lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts / AssistantStream.ts for the higher-level helper classes.I now have a complete picture. Let me check the realtime websocket streaming briefly since it's architecturally distinct (not SSE-based).Confirmed: realtime uses raw WebSocket, entirely separate from the SSE `Stream` machinery. I have enough to answer comprehensively.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE engine — `src/core/streaming.ts`**
- `class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` — the fundamental streaming primitive returned by every streaming SDK call.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — turns a `fetch` `Response` into an async-iterable stream of parsed JSON events (handles `[DONE]` sentinel, per-event JSON parsing, error surfacing via `APIError`).
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — alternate constructor for newline-delimited JSON streams (used by `.toReadableStream()`/round-tripping).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / `class SSEDecoder` — low-level SSE framing: splits bytes on the double-newline event boundary and parses `event:`/`data:` fields into `ServerSentEvent`.
- Depends on `src/internal/decoders/line.ts` (`LineDecoder`, `findDoubleNewlineIndex`) for byte-to-line decoding across chunk boundaries.
- `src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export shim (`export * from './core/streaming'`).

**Dispatch point — `src/internal/parse.ts`**
`defaultParseResponse()` checks `props.options.stream`; if true it calls either a per-request `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (used when a resource needs a custom Stream subclass) or the default `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client)`. This is the single chokepoint where every raw HTTP client call becomes a `Stream` instead of a parsed JSON body. It's wired into request handling in `src/client.ts` (the base `OpenAI` client's `buildRequest`/fetch pipeline).

**Higher-level ergonomic wrappers (built on top of `Stream`)**
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — `EventStream` base class adding `.on(event, cb)`-style event emission over a raw `Stream`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` + `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk`s into a final `ChatCompletion`, powers `client.chat.completions.stream()` and `.runTools()` (streaming variant).
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` (with `ResponseAccumulator.ts`, `EventTypes.ts`) — accumulates Responses API SSE events into a snapshot `Response`, powers `client.responses.stream()`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — the Assistants (beta) equivalent, powers `client.beta.threads.runs.stream()` / `.createAndStream()`.

**Separate, non-SSE streaming path**
`src/realtime/websocket.ts`, `src/realtime/ws.ts`, `src/realtime/internal-base.ts` implement the Realtime API over a raw `WebSocket` (`OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket extends OpenAIRealtimeEmitter`) — this does not go through `core/streaming.ts` at all; it's an independent transport.

## Public API methods that route into it

| Method | File | Return type |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` / `.retrieve({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.stream(...)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:201` → `lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` | `ResponseStream<ParsedT>` (EventStream wrapper) |
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(...)` | `completions.ts:221-225` → `lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` | `ChatCompletionStream<ParsedT>` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(...)` (stream variant) | `completions.ts:195-216` → `lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner<ParsedT>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` / `.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent \| ImageGenStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:31-50` | `APIPromise<Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` (deprecated) | `runs.ts:165-234` → `lib/AssistantStream.ts` | `AssistantStream` |
| `new OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket(...)` | `src/realtime/websocket.ts` | separate WebSocket transport, not `Stream` |

All of the `create({stream:true})` overloads share the same mechanism: they call `this._client.post(...)`/`.get(...)` with `stream: true` in the request options, which `client.ts` forwards to `internal/parse.ts`'s `defaultParseResponse`, which calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (`core/streaming.ts`). The `.stream()` convenience methods (`responses.stream`, `chat.completions.stream`, `beta.threads.runs.stream`) are thin wrappers that call the same underlying `create` request internally but return an `EventStream` subclass instead of a raw `Stream`.

**Not verified:** I did not read `src/client.ts` end-to-end (only grepped for `stream`/`__streamClass` occurrences) to trace exactly how `__streamClass` is threaded from a resource method into `RequestOptions`, nor did I read `lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`, `lib/AssistantStream.ts`, or `lib/ResponsesParser.ts` in full — only their entry points and imports. I also did not check `resources/beta/chatkit` or `resources/containers` for any additional streaming surfaces beyond what's listed.

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

```sh
npm install openai
```

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
```

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```
